records.label: Use classification as backbone
records.details: Use NAPCS for Canadian/economic classification, GS1 GPC for retail/product categories, and UNSPSC for procurement categories.

records.label: Use open barcode databases first
records.details: Open Food Facts is the strongest open barcode source. Open Products/Beauty/Pet Food Facts add non-food categories but coverage varies.

records.label: Use GS1 Canada where access is possible
records.details: ECCnet is likely the most valuable Canadian product-content source, but it requires proper access. Treat it as a high-value target.

records.label: Use paid barcode APIs only as enrichment
records.details: UPCitemdb, Go-UPC, Barcode Lookup and Big Product Data can fill product identity gaps, but should not replace official/open sources.

records.label: Create identity-to-offer linkage
records.details: Separate ProductIdentity records from RetailOffer rows. The same barcode/GTIN can map to many sellers, stores, prices and availability snapshots.
